anchors.1: Fails the task or contradicts essential supplied facts.
anchors.2: Partly relevant, but requires substantial revision or loses the voice.
anchors.3: Usable with revision; meets the main task with visible weaknesses.
anchors.4: Strong, purposeful response; minor editorial changes needed.
anchors.5: Excellent for this brief; precise, convincing and distinctive.

instructions: Judge the task-specific rubric; do not reward length or ornate prose on their own.
Give each answer an overall 1–5 rating informed by the applicable dimensions; compare A/B and record a reason.
Mark tie when neither answer is meaningfully better.
Flag invented canon, quotation errors, unwanted edits and copied-looking text.
Use at least two reviewers on a representative subset and adjudicate disagreement.
Keep model identities and private-key.json away from reviewers.
Do not use benchmark scenarios or reviewer targets as training examples.

review.notes: Draft anchors and review protocol; requires editorial approval before freezing.
